Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Per our discussion, attaching a quick context/token profile (tabbed by feature) so your team can size models and estimate token spend. High-level notes below: 

- Product scope: document summarization (short reports ~1-3 pages), intelligent highlights for long contracts (~10–40 pages), and inline question answering for support transcripts (avg 1.2k tokens per session).
- Peak concurrency: 120 simultaneous end-users expected in month 1; target P95 latency under 600ms for interactive features.
- Context mix: 60% short summaries (≤1k tokens), 30% contract QnA (~4–12k tokens depending on document retrieval strategy), 10% long transcript sessions (up to 8k tokens).
- Security: SOC2 in progress; we will need audit log samples and runbook for data retention.

Attached: blueharbor_context_token_profile.xlsx (feature tabs + hourly spike traces).

Can Redwood propose a short list of model variants (cost vs latency trade-offs) and a recommended rollout plan (pilot -> canary -> GA)?

Best,
Lena Park
Head of Product
BlueHarbor Analytics

Attachment: blueharbor_context_token_profile.xlsx (xlsx)

Hi Lena — thanks for the profile, that spreadsheet was very helpful. Quick response with a suggested starting shortlist and a few clarifying questions so we size correctly: 

Shortlist (initial candidates):
- rw-m-7b-int8 (low-cost, best for high-concurrency summary endpoints)
- rw-s-13b-fp16 (balanced quality/latency for contract QnA)
- rw-l-34b-q4 (high-quality for long-context transcript threading where precision matters)

Key assumptions we made from your spreadsheet: 
- Average tokens per short summary: 750 (prompt+response).
- Contract QnA typical context window: planning for 8k context; we assume retrieval returns top-3 docs trimmed to ~6k tokens before prompting.
- Transcript sessions: long sessions will be windowed and summarized incrementally; plan for 4–6k rolling context per active session.

Questions: 
1) For contract QnA, will BlueHarbor prefer full-document context in a single pass (single long prompt) or iterative retrieval + chain-of-thought style prompts? This impacts which model we recommend.
2) Do you have any hard latency SLAs for contract QnA? We noted interactive SLA target of P95 < 600ms but long-context queries can be higher.

Connor from our implementation team is cc'd and will propose throughput numbers based on your concurrency profile. Monica will own the rollout checklist and compliance artifacts.

--
Irene Choi
Sr. Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Hi Lena — Connor here (CS-Eng). I sketched a throughput and token-bucket estimate for the three shortlisted model classes and attached a short PDF with per-model qps and expected cost ranges. Highlights: 

- rw-m-7b-int8 (best-effort low-latency): single-GPU instances can sustain ~350 qps for 1k-token end-to-end prompts with batching; recommended to run this on Dedicated pools with autoscaling to handle your 120 concurrent users plus burst.
- rw-s-13b-fp16: sweet spot for 2–4k context; expect ~80–120 qps per GPU depending on batch sizing and KV-cache hit-rate. Plan for 2–3x headroom if you want P95 < 600ms for 4k prompts.
- rw-l-34b-q4: high-quality but expensive; for 6–8k rolling context, estimate ~12–25 qps per GPU. Use as a fallthrough model for complex QnA or for privacy-sensitive workflows.

Token-bucket quick math (month 1, rough):
- Short summaries: 60% * 120 users * avg 4 calls/day * 750 tokens = ~2.16M tokens/day
- Contract QnA (interactive): 30% * 120 users * avg 10 calls/day * 4k tokens = ~1.44M tokens/day
- Transcript sessions: 10% * 120 users * avg 2 sessions/day * 5k tokens = ~0.12M tokens/day
- Total ~3.7M tokens/day -> ~111M tokens/month (buffer to 140M for spikes)

Operational recommendations:
- Pilot with rw-m-7b-int8 for summaries and rw-s-13b-fp16 for contract QnA; enable prefix/KV caching for repeated doc queries to reduce effective token cost.
- Canary the 34b model on 5% of queries that fail a quality threshold (we can wire a fallback rule).
- Precompute embeddings and store chunk-level metadata to minimize retrieval token overhead for contract QnA.

Attachment: redwood_model_shortlist_and_metrics.pdf (3 pages) — includes per-model latency/cost curves and baseline qps.

Thanks everyone — great threading of the plan. Lena, below is a compact implementation runbook and next steps so we can lock week 1 tasks: 

Week 0 (prep)
- RD: review attached deployment-runbook-draft.md and confirm SOC2 evidence points (audit log retention, KMS integration windows).
- BH: share sample contract retrieval pipeline (doc chunk size, retrieval latency) so we can validate tokenizer vs chunk boundaries.

Week 1 (pilot)
- Deploy rw-m-7b-int8 on a dedicated pool for summaries. Run smoke tests (50 users simulated, 95th percentile latency target check).
- Deploy rw-s-13b-fp16 for contract QnA with retrieval pipeline; enable KV caching and monitor token burn.
- Start traffic mirroring for rw-l-34b-q4 on 5% of contract queries to collect quality deltas.

Metrics to capture (dashboard):
- P50/P95 latency per endpoint, tokens per request, KV cache hit-rate, cost per 1k tokens, failure/retry rate.
- A weekly quality check: 200 sampled QnA responses scored vs. expected ground truth (BlueHarbor to provide annotator).

Docs & links: attached runbook + model shortlist PDF and your original token profile. I'll open a HubSpot task for weekly checkpoints and a shared Drive folder for artifacts.

Next steps: if this looks good, confirm the SOC2 evidence timeline and we’ll schedule a 60-minute pilot kickoff for Oct 4th.

Cheers,
Monica Patel
Implementation Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachment: deployment-runbook-draft.md (md)
